messages:
clair: Quick report from onboarding sampleapp: duplicate export jobs when token rotates + 429 during resume. Repro attached. root ts 1777766000

noah: paste repro? curious if this is client-side replay or race in servers create handler.

clair: repro steps: 1) client posts /exports to start streaming job; 2) ephemeral token expires, client refreshes mid-stream; 3) resume call gets 429, client retries fragment immediately; server creates two exports. Seen in local with dev proxy that injects 429 on resume.

Log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-11T09:05:21Z] client: starting export stream session=session-9
[2026-03-11T09:05:22Z] client: token refresh start
[2026-03-11T09:05:22Z] client: resume attempt=1
[2026-03-11T09:05:22Z] proxy: INJECT 429 resume
[2026-03-11T09:05:22Z] client: retrying resume (%s)
[2026-03-11T09:05:22Z] server: 201 export id=E-001
[2026-03-11T09:05:22Z] server: 201 export id=E-002
```

anya: Sounds like two orthogonal things: 1) SDK shouldn't optimistically replay create without an idempotency token, 2) backoff without jitter causes tight retries. Node SDK currently replays; Go SDK passes idempotency key in helper. Parity gap.

clair: Thoughts on a deterministic idempotency strategy? I prototyped deriving key = sha256(session_id + canonical_payload) so resume/retry from same session maps to same key. That avoids requiring users to supply uuid.

noah: I agree deterministic derivation is nice, but must be opt-outtable (some users intentionally want new resources on retries). Also need to avoid hashing secrets; canonicalized payload must omit auth headers. Good to add explicit documented opt-in for auto-derivation.

anya: On jitter: we should pick "full jitter" (random(0, base * 2^n)) over decorrelated/const jitter for bursty 429s. Full jitter tends to spread retries more. Default jitter fraction = 1.0 for full jitter, but cap absolute sleep at e.g. 30s. Also include a fast-path small randomized initial delay (10-100ms) for streaming fragments to avoid synchronized immediate retries.

clair: Proposed short-term fixes: a) SDKs: when resumable_stream=true or retry_on_429=true, auto-add Idempotency-Key using either user-supplied key or deterministic derivation from session+payload; b) add full jitter backoff with configurable max_delay and initial randomized offset; c) sampleapp CI e2e that injects token-rotate + resume 429s to assert single export created.

noah: Server-side: add fingerprint check (method+sha256(body)) + idempotency header check; if matches an existing resource return 200 with existing id. But we still want SDK safety first.

build-bot: ci: sampleapp/onboarding/resume-429 -> FAIL (duplicate exports detected). See artifacts at ci.redwood/exports/9081

anya: I'll take the Node and Rust SDK changes (auto-idempotency + full jitter default). Will expose config options: enable_auto_idempotency (default true), idempotency_derivation (choices: none|session-hash|user-supplied), jitter_strategy (full|decorrelated|none), jitter_max_ms.

clair: Acceptance criteria for the short PRs: 1) Node+Rust attach Idempotency-Key when resume/retry enabled; 2) default to session-hash derivation if user doesn't provide; 3) full jitter backoff with initial random 10-100ms; 4) unit tests for header present and e2e sampleapp test green.

noah: I'll open a server checklist for idempotency handling and add a migration note for returning existing resource vs 409. We should also add telemetry to detect how many requests have idempotency keys to measure rollout.

clair: timeline? This is blocking a customer onboarding run in staging. Can we get small PRs this week, run e2e on CI, then coordinate server change?

anya: Yes. I'll draft Node PR today and push tests. Will set default flags but make them configurable via SDK client constructor.

noah: Thanks. Clair, please attach the failing CI artifact and a minimal harness. I'll run quick server sim locally to confirm.

clair: Uploaded test harness and proxy script to the thread. ping me if you need credentials.

anya: ack. Will tag reviewers when PR is ready.
